standing: HELD — Akien's spec, captured mid-design across three sharpenings in one conversation. Not cast, not built. Recorded because it lived nowhere but a chat window, which is the Law 1 defect the whole system exists to stop.
why_held: The ruling arrived in three passes, each one loosening the previous. Building against pass one would have been building against a spec that no longer existed by pass three. This file is what the ticketer reads before casting, so the cast is against the settled shape.

akien_verbatim.said: workflow versions would be meaningless. a workflow is composed at ticketing time by the ticketer based on the needs of the ticket.
_registered_workflow?! There shouldn't be one! _conform sounds wrong too! and there are no workflow_versions. so whatever has to be rebuilt gets rebuilt.

lets revisit what should be on a ticket. it should list it's workflow. what gates and what things it will require to pass those gates. the gates themselves only see the boats that meet their criteria. that's the only thing to check. can i pass? do you have the pass that matches the pass you're supposed to have? Yes? Ok! else no, send back to author

no, the ticket's author declares the workflow ON the ticket based on the needs of the ticket. what's the difference between a task and a ticket? it's terminal state. that's all. the terminal state for a ticket is in the code, and the terminal state for a task is done and the artifact disappearing in 30 days along with expired logs. literally ANY WORKFLOW AT ALL, WITH MULTIPLE LOOPS AND SWIRLS, COULD THEORETICALLY BE PUT ON A TICKET. And the system would do it's best to accomodate and flag when it couldn't back to the author.

the_settled_shape.who_owns_the_workflow: THE TICKET'S AUTHOR, on the ticket, composed for the needs of that ticket. Not the class. There is no registered path, no version of a path, and nothing for an instance to conform to.
the_settled_shape.what_a_workflow_is: A GRAPH, not a path. Any workflow at all — multiple loops and swirls — is legal to put on a ticket. The plainest form that holds all of it is a list of EDGES ({from, to}); nodes are implied and a terminal node is one with no way out. The existing 'A -> B -> [C] -> D' arrow string stays as the rendering of the common case (a chain IS a graph), so no existing ticket has to be rewritten to keep working.
the_settled_shape.what_a_gate_checks: ONE question, in Akien's words: 'can i pass? do you have the pass that matches the pass you're supposed to have?' Yes -> through. No -> SEND BACK TO AUTHOR. A gate never adjudicates the path; there is nothing to conform to. 'The gates themselves only see the boats that meet their criteria.'
the_settled_shape.who_owns_the_criteria: THE GATE owns the criteria; the TICKET owns the pass it presents. CC's read, resolved by Law 6 rather than referred to Akien: a boat that declares its own sufficiency is not passing a gate, it is self-certifying. The ticket names WHERE its pass is; the gate goes and checks the pass is real and green. Declaring is not certifying.
the_settled_shape.ticket_vs_task: TERMINAL STATE, and that is ALL — same machinery, same author-declared graph, two destinations. A TICKET's terminal is IN THE CODE. A TASK's terminal is done, with the artifact disappearing in 30 days along with expired logs.
the_settled_shape.failure_posture: ACCOMMODATE AND FLAG, not refuse-on-drift. The system does its best to service whatever graph the author drew, and flags back to the AUTHOR what it could not do. This inverts today's posture, where an unrecognized shape is refused as drifted.
the_settled_shape.no_gate_does_work: Akien, 2026-08-03 pass 5: 'so my idea was the build inspector was part of the build skill (sail)'. THE GATE NEVER DOES THE WORK — it reads the receipt. Today emit() reaches into the component at the crossing's own address and RUNS build_inspector at crossing time; that reach IS the managing Akien named ('you had checks in the components... managing, rather than letting the things self manage'). Under his idea the work happens where the work happens: /sail builds and /sail inspects, then presents the pass. This generalizes to every gate with no exception, which is how it is known to be the pattern and not a fix for one gate — /chart produces the charted-course pass, whatever arms a probe produces that one. A gate matches, always.
the_settled_shape.the_pass_already_exists: A VALIDATION IS THE PASS — not invented, found in-house (borrow-patterns: check in-house first). cairn/tester/validation_store.py::persist_validation is a single APPEND-ONLY write-door that refuses anything but the ratified eight fields (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, +2) and stores the record BESIDE what it seals. verdict: 'green'. build_inspector already writes them (cairn/build_inspector/validations/*.json). The gate was not failing to have a pass — it was re-doing the work instead of reading the one already on disk.
the_settled_shape.a_pass_can_go_stale: CC's read, resolved rather than handed back: a green validation from three weeks and forty commits ago is not a current pass. Also already-solved in-house — CLAUDE.md gives a host-seam an EXPIRING seal precisely because 'the host drifts with nothing in git changing'. Same rule applied uniformly: the pass names WHAT it sealed and WHEN, and the gate checks the sealed thing has not moved since. Not a new mechanism; the existing one, everywhere.

the_reconciliation_that_keeps_law_8: Accommodate-and-flag opens a hole on its face: if the author composes the route, an author can compose a route around every gate, and 'accommodate' would mean the system watches it happen. Akien's own terminal-state ruling closes it. THE ROUTE IS THE AUTHOR'S; THE TERMINAL STATES ARE THE SYSTEM'S. Swirl however you like — a ticket's terminal is IN THE CODE, and landing in the codebase is exactly where the pass is checked. The author cannot compose past it because the author does not own the destination. So a cast-time flag ('nothing in this workflow will check X') is an honest report the author owns, not silent permission. CC's read, not ruled.
already_encoded_in_the_roots: The ticket/task terminal split is NOT new placement — CLAUDE.md's three-roots table already puts each where it belongs. A ticket stages in CairnCommons/tickets/ and MIGRATES BESIDE THE CODE to become that component's history (terminal = in the code). ~/.cairn/ is instance-space, 'logs, credentials, flags, cached state', never in git (terminal = done, gone with the expired logs). Derived, not invented. What does NOT exist yet is the 30-day expiry mechanism itself.
what_dies: workflow_versions — on node_classes/code-seam.json and skill.json (the only two that carry any). The class keeps what, why, invariant, prove_gate, extra_gates, kicks_back_on, members: it still owns WHAT PROVES A MEMBER, just not the path one walks.
transitions._registered_workflow — refuses a version the class does not define; there are no versions.
transitions._conform — path-equality against a registered path; there is no registered path.
skippable_summons — a workaround for a fork a linear list cannot draw. A composed graph draws the fork.
free_summons — a workaround for a repeat a linear list cannot draw. A composed graph draws the loop.
transitions.resolve_target's nearest-occurrence-forward-first rule — a name is ambiguous only because a list cannot hold a loop. In a graph you traverse an edge.
the @vN in the 'class@version:' header — a version OF the class's workflow, which no longer exists.
'direction' and 'severity' as DERIVED facts in the emit record — both are cursor-index arithmetic and a graph has no index. If severity matters it becomes a property the author puts on an edge.

emit_migrated / migrate_to_v2 — v1->v2 migration doors. With no versions there is nothing to migrate between. NOTE: this also dissolves the open trouble a-boat-resting-in-a-dissolved-state-has-no-door-out, whose whole subject is a boat stuck between versions.
what_dies_under_no_gate_does_work: transitions._build_gate — the chokepoint's reach into a component address to RUN build_inspector at crossing time. The inspector moves into /sail (the build skill), where the building happens; the gate reads the validation /sail persisted.

the LAZY IMPORT of build_inspector inside transitions.py — it exists ONLY because the chokepoint summons the inspector, and the module header calls out the boot-order care it needed. No reach, no import, no boot-order care.
the whole PROVEME special case in emit(), and by the same argument the BUILDME / PROVED / WATCHME special cases: five named states the chokepoint had to know about become zero.

_EXEMPT_ROSTER — an exemption mechanism built ahead of any entry (measured 2026-08-03: EMPTY, and the only one in the file). A gate that reads a receipt has nothing to exempt; a boat either carries a current pass or it does not.

measured_before_the_cut.why_recorded: Law 3 — the claim 'this simplifies everything' is a hypothesis until the after-number exists. This is the before-number, so the rebuild can be judged rather than felt.

what_survives: The -ME grammar (a state ending in -ME is a SUMMONS, demanding a peer; else a rest) — classless, derivable, and orthogonal to who composed the graph.

The five gates' CRITERIA — what each one requires — but NOT their work. The work moves to whoever owns it (build_inspector into /sail, per Akien pass 5). What is left at the chokepoint is one table lookup and one refusal shape. The bespoke-exemption-per-gate pattern is where intentions-model-compiler slipped through with no watch and nothing objected.
cairn/tester/validation_store.py — untouched. It was already the pass door; it simply gains readers.
load_class_def — an unknown class is still refused (Law 8: an unknown class has no physics).
The append door and everything downstream of the journal (Law 7 untouched).
what_must_be_built: The edge-list workflow form, alongside the arrow-string rendering for chains.
The pass block on a ticket: per gate on its graph, what the ticket presents.
The gate table: gate name -> criteria it owns -> the one admit check -> one refusal shape (send back to author).
The cast-time accommodation report: what the system can service on this graph and what it cannot, delivered to the author.
The task terminal: 30-day artifact expiry tied to log expiry, in instance-space.
open_and_deliberately_unanswered: Whether a task's 30-day expiry is a real clock or an event (Cairn's standing aim is event-fired, never a poll — see the shrinking-footprint line). 'Expiring along with expired logs' suggests it rides the LOG expiry as its event rather than owning a timer, which would be the event-shaped answer. Not ruled; noted so the builder does not reach for cron by reflex.
kin: CairnCommons/tickets/ticket-and-task.json — cast 2026-07-22, Akien-ratified 'agreed!', cursor at BUILDME. Its subject IS the ticket/task distinction, and pass 4 above SETTLES it: the differentiator is terminal state, that is all. This note is that ticket's answer, not a rival.
